## Step 1: Develop initial scraper and crawler

```{python}
BASE_URL = "https://oig.hhs.gov"
START_URL = "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"
HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "DAP30538CourseBot/1.0 (jpacher@uchicago.edu)"}
DATE_PAT = re.compile(r"^[A-Z][a-z]+ \d{1,2}, \d{4}$")
```

```{python}
resp = requests.get(START_URL, headers=HEADERS, timeout=30)

resp.raise_for_status()

soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "html.parser") #could not install lxml

rows = []
```

```{python}
for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
    href = a["href"]

    if not (href.startswith("/fraud/enforcement/") and href != "/fraud/enforcement/"):
        continue

    title = a.get_text(strip=True)
    link = urljoin(BASE_URL, href)

    container = a.find_parent(["li", "article", "div"])
    if container is None:
        continue

    text_lines = [t.strip() for t in container.stripped_strings if t.strip()]

    date = None
    date_idx = None
    for i, t in enumerate(text_lines):
        if DATE_PAT.match(t):
            date = t
            date_idx = i
            break

    categories = []
    if date_idx is not None:

        for t in text_lines[date_idx + 1:]:
            if t == title:
                continue

            categories.append(t)

    category = "; ".join(categories) if categories else None

    if date is None:
        continue

    rows.append({"title": title, "date": date, "category": category, "link": link})

df = pd.DataFrame(rows).drop_duplicates(subset=["title", "date", "link"]).reset_index(drop=True)

print(df.head())

```

## Step 2: Making the scraper dynamic

### 1. Turning the scraper into a function 

* a. Pseudo-Code

- Print a message if the input year is less than 2013 and stop execution.

- Create a cutoff date corresponding to the first day of the requested month and year.

- Initialize page = 1 and an empty list to store all scraped enforcement actions.

- Use a while loop to crawl pages:

  - Fetch the HTML for the current page and locate enforcement action cards.

  - If no cards are found, stop crawling.

  - For each card, extract the title, date, category, and link, convert the date to a comparable format, and store the result.

  - If the oldest date on the page is earlier than the cutoff date, stop crawling.

  - Otherwise, wait briefly and move to the next page.

- Convert the collected records into a tidy dataframe, save it as enforcement_actions_year_month.csv, and return the dataframe.

(I used AI to help me write my pseudo code, I frist write it up and after I asked him to correct it.)

* b. Create Dynamic Scraper

```{python}

def crawl_enforcement_actions(start_month: int, start_year: int, sleep_seconds: int = 1) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Crawl pages until reaching start_month/start_year, then return rows since cutoff."""
    if start_year < 2013:
        print("Please use year >= 2013. Enforcement actions are listed from 2013 onward.")
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["title", "date", "category", "link", "date_parsed"])

    cutoff = datetime(start_year, start_month, 1)

    page = 1
    all_pages = []

    while True:
        df_page = parse_one_page(page)

        if df_page.empty:
            break

        df_page["date_parsed"] = pd.to_datetime(df_page["date"], format="%B %d, %Y", errors="coerce")
        all_pages.append(df_page)

        oldest_on_page = df_page["date_parsed"].min()
        if pd.notna(oldest_on_page) and oldest_on_page < cutoff:
            break

        time.sleep(sleep_seconds)
        page += 1

    if not all_pages:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["title", "date", "category", "link", "date_parsed"])

    df_all = pd.concat(all_pages, ignore_index=True)
    df_all = df_all[df_all["date_parsed"] >= cutoff].copy()
    df_all = df_all.sort_values("date_parsed", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

    return df_all

RUN_SCRAPER = False

start_month = 1
start_year = 2024
csv_name = f"enforcement_actions_{start_year}_{start_month:02d}.csv"

if RUN_SCRAPER:
    df_2024 = crawl_enforcement_actions(start_month, start_year, sleep_seconds=1)
    df_2024.to_csv(csv_name, index=False)
else:
    df_2024 = pd.read_csv(csv_name)
    df_2024["date_parsed"] = pd.to_datetime(df_2024["date"], format="%B %d, %Y", errors="coerce")

#df_2024.head()
```

## Step 3: Plot data based on scraped data

```{python}
# Load the CSV created in Step 2
df = pd.read_csv(
    "enforcement_actions_2022_01.csv",
    parse_dates=["date"]
)

# Create year-month variable for aggregation
df["year_month"] = df["date"].dt.to_period("M").dt.to_timestamp()

#df.head()

```

### 1. Plot the number of enforcement actions over time

```{python}
monthly_counts = (
    df.groupby("year_month")
      .size()
      .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)

chart_total = (
    alt.Chart(monthly_counts)
    .mark_line(point=True)
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month-Year"),
        y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Enforcement Actions"),
        tooltip=["year_month:T", "n_actions:Q"]
    )
    .properties(
        title="HHS OIG Enforcement Actions Over Time (Since Jan 2022)",
        width=500,
        height=300
    )
)

chart_total

```

* based on five topics

```{python}
def classify_topic(title):
    t = title.lower()

    if any(k in t for k in ["health", "medicare", "medicaid", "hospital", "physician", "clinic"]):
        return "Health Care Fraud"
    elif any(k in t for k in ["bank", "financial", "loan", "credit", "wire", "securities"]):
        return "Financial Fraud"
    elif any(k in t for k in ["drug", "opioid", "pharma", "controlled substance"]):
        return "Drug Enforcement"
    elif any(k in t for k in ["bribe", "bribery", "corrupt", "kickback"]):
        return "Bribery/Corruption"
    else:
        return "Other"

```

```{python}
df_cc = df[df["category"] == "Criminal and Civil Actions"].copy()
df_cc["topic"] = df_cc["title"].apply(classify_topic)

monthly_topics = (
    df_cc.groupby(["year_month", "topic"])
         .size()
         .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)

```

```{python}
chart_topics = (
    alt.Chart(monthly_topics)
    .mark_line(point=True)
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month-Year"),
        y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Enforcement Actions"),

)
```
